goal: replace the per-figure human content decision, which does not reach 15,600 patents
training_data: the 158 curated decisions (100 in scope, 58 out of scope)

attempt_1_image_features.model: frozen ResNet18 ImageNet features, 512-d, plus a logistic probe
attempt_1_image_features.verdict: FAILS the 95% acceptance test. Even auto-deciding only the most confident 42% gives 87.9%, short of the 98% precision a non-human authority needs.

attempt_2_pipeline_features.features: 20 Stage-0 to Stage-3 quantities plus four shape ratios (closed-edge fraction, hachure fraction, labels per edge, hatch-primitive fraction)
attempt_2_pipeline_features.verdict: WORSE than image features. Ran the 58 rejected figures through the pipeline to obtain features for both classes, so the comparison is fair.

conclusion: Both approaches fail, and by a wide margin rather than narrowly. The task is harder than it looks: a mechanical cross-section and a block diagram are both thin black lines on white, and the distinction is semantic. 158 examples is too few for either representation to learn it.
consequence: Content routing stays human-gated, which makes Phase D -- not anything in the pipeline -- the binding constraint on corpus scale.
recommendation: The fix is labels, not a better model. tools/curate_pilot.py already works and is resumable; roughly 1000 decisions at a few seconds each is one to two hours of curation, and is the cheapest path to a usable authority. Training on 158 and hoping is not.
